result.scope: The scalar radial bound fails at this selected correlation. The elementary correction repairs the profile at 1/2; the sharp local first-moment correction repairs it also at 3/5 but fails at 7/10. Positive upper-bound coefficients do not prove improving Gaussian partitions. Finite Gram controls support the written algebraic lemma, not an unrestricted proof by sampling.

certified_scope: At rho=1/2 the bounded exactly mean-zero function f=exp(-t)+2exp(-16t)-21/34 violates the scalar radial inequality. The elementary Gamma correction repairs its small profile at1/2 but fails at3/5. The sharp first-moment correction repairs the same small profile at3/5 but has a strictly positive upper-bound coefficient at7/10. None of the positive coefficients proves an improving partition.
analytic_scope: DG6 proves the all-profile Gram bound and coupled angular inequality. DG8 gives a globally valid positive-part matrix refinement, sharp among norm-and-closure bounds near balanced profiles, with local coefficient1/8. Its Taylor expansion and the directed coefficients prove the restricted-profile comparisons. These analytic assertions are written proofs, not claims of unrestricted verification from finite controls.
arithmetic_scope: All infinite radial integrals are reduced analytically to closed quadrant formulas. Arb encloses every angular integrand on each of 8192 intervals, at 100-bit precision; no sampled angular rule or omitted radial tail is used.
limits: The original all-positive-correlation goal remains open. Profile comparisons at1/2 and3/5 concern sufficiently small multiples of one explicit circular-mass profile with arbitrary angular shapes. Failure of the separated-first-moment upper bound at7/10 is a limitation of that sufficient criterion, not a counterexample to simplex optimality. The unrestricted global cutoff remains21/50.
